newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian supply craft blasts off on schedule.
newsitem.headline: Russian supply craft blasts off on schedule.

text.p: A Russian Progress-35 cargo craft blasted off on Saturday with an emergency repair kit, oxygen reserves, food and water for the crippled Mir orbiting station.
Docking with the Mir is expected on Monday.
Reporters tracked the movements of the craft on screens at mission control in Korolyov near Moscow.
Officials gathered in front of the screens applauded when Progress separated from the booster at an altitude of around 200 km (125 miles).

Progress was carrying 1.5 tonnes of supplies for the Mir space station, which has two Russians and an American abroad and lost up to half its electric power in a collision with an earlier unmanned supply craft on June 25.

"The crew is expecting special equipment from the Earth which will help them to make a visit to the damaged Spektr module," Viktor Blagov, deputy flight director, said on Friday, adding that parcels from the crew's families were also on board.
